los.text: Identify the clinical signs of cardiac arrest
los.html:
SignDetail
UnresponsiveNo response to voice or a shake of the shoulders
Not breathing normallyAbsent breathing or agonal gasps (slow, noisy, irregular: common in the first minutes, treat as cardiac arrest)
No signs of lifeNo movement, coughing or normal breathing; healthcare staff may also feel for a carotid pulse (no more than 10 seconds)
CheckOpen the airway (head tilt, chin lift), then look, listen and feel for no more than 10 seconds.
If in doubt, start CPRa brief seizure-like episode or gasping can be the first sign of arrest.

los.text: Demonstrate effective adult CPR in accordance with current guidelines
los.html:
1. DangerMake sure you, the casualty and bystanders are safe.
2. Response"Are you all right?", shake gently by the shoulders.
3Shout for help, then Airway: head tilt, chin lift.
4. BreathingLook, listen, feel for up to 10 seconds.
5Call 999 / 2222 (hospital), ask someone to fetch an AED; use speakerphone.
6. 30 compressionsCentre of the chest (lower half of sternum), 5–6 cm deep, 100–120/min, full recoil, minimal interruptions.
72 rescue breaths (if trained and willing), each ~1 second, enough to make the chest rise.
8Continue 30:2; attach the AED as soon as it arrives and follow its prompts; swap compressors every 2 minutes.
  • Guidelines: Resuscitation Council UK (2021). Compression-only CPR is acceptable if unwilling or unable to give breaths.

los.text: Describe the key components of a medical history and explain their significance.
los.html:
SectionWhat it coversWhy it matters
Presenting complaintThe problem in the patient's wordsFocuses the consultation
History of presenting complaintOnset, duration, character, progression, associated symptoms, red flags (e.g. SOCRATES for pain)Most diagnoses come from the history
Past medical/surgical historyConditions, operations, hospital admissionsRisk factors, recurrence, contraindications
Drug historyPrescribed, over-the-counter, herbal, recreational; allergies and the reactionSide effects, interactions, safe prescribing
Family historyIllness in first-degree relativesInherited risk
Social historySmoking (pack-years), alcohol (units), occupation, home, function, drivingRisk factors, impact, discharge planning
Systems reviewBrief screen of other systemsPicks up missed problems
ICEIdeas, concerns, expectationsPatient-centred care, shared decisions

los.text: Summarise patient history findings and communicate them effectively during clinical handover or presentations.
los.html:
• Structure: use SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) for handover, or a case presentation order for ward rounds.
Case presentationExample
Opening line"Mr X, 64, presented with 3 days of bloody diarrhoea."
HPCKey positives and important negatives
PMH, drugs, allergies, socialOnly what is relevant
SummaryOne sentence pulling it together
Differential and planMost likely first; next investigations
  • Tips: be concise, put the most important point first, avoid jargon, check the listener has understood, and document clearly.

los.text: Evaluate the role of medical history in diagnosis and patient management.
los.html:
• The history gives about 70–80% of diagnoses; examination and tests mainly confirm or refine.
RoleExample
Generates a differential diagnosisPattern of symptoms, timing, risk factors
Guides examination and investigationsAvoids unnecessary tests
Identifies red flags and urgencyWeight loss and rectal bleeding → urgent cancer referral
Informs managementAllergies, drug interactions, frailty, patient wishes
Builds rapport and trustBetter adherence and shared decisions
